tasks.title: Preserve interrupted restore staging and support safe retry
prerequisites: Keep the original backup immutable and restore only to a new destination
acceptance: A simulated hard interruption after one verified copy preserves an INTERRUPTED staging directory
An interruption manifest records verified files and explicit recovery guidance
KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit semantics are preserved after evidence is written
A retry from the original verified backup into a new destination succeeds
The interrupted stage and original backup are not overwritten or silently deleted
tasks.note: restore_source_backup now catches BaseException only to preserve staging evidence, writes restore-interruption.json and atomically renames the stage to INTERRUPTED-*, then re-raises KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit unchanged. Ordinary exceptions retain FAILED-* plus BackupError behavior. Test simulates KeyboardInterrupt after one copied file, verifies metadata and preserved stage, then retries from the original backup into a new destination. This does not catch SIGKILL or power loss; those require durable orphan-stage detection/lease design.

tasks.title: Design safe orphan staging detection after uncatchable process termination
prerequisites: Inspect current backup/restore staging names and manifests
Define a concurrency-safe lock or lease so an active restore is not misclassified
acceptance: SIGKILL/power-loss orphan stages can be distinguished from active work
Recovery never promotes an incomplete stage to a complete restore
Recovery never overwrites or deletes an existing backup or restore
Orphan stages remain inspectable with actionable metadata
Tests cover active lease, expired lease, malformed marker, and retry
tasks.note: Python cannot catch SIGKILL or power loss. Do not add a naive startup scan that might rename another live restore's staging directory.
